title: Kubernetes Deployment
summary: Kubernetes runs on desired state. You declare what you want ('3 replicas of v2'), the API server stores it in etcd, and independent controllers each watch for differences between desired and actual state and act to close the gap. A Deployment rollout is many small loops cooperating: the Deployment controller creates pods, the scheduler places them, and kubelets run them, all coordinating through the API server.

walkthrough.title: Apply a Deployment
walkthrough.text: kubectl apply (or a GitOps controller) sends the Deployment manifest with the new image v2 and replicas: 3 to the API server.

walkthrough.title: Validate and persist
walkthrough.text: The API server authenticates the request, checks RBAC, runs admission webhooks (e.g. 'images must be signed'), and stores the object in etcd, which replicates it with Raft.

walkthrough.title: Controller creates a ReplicaSet
walkthrough.text: The Deployment controller, watching Deployments, sees the new template. It creates a v2 ReplicaSet and scales it up while scaling v1 down, within maxSurge and maxUnavailable.

walkthrough.title: Scheduler places pods
walkthrough.text: The scheduler watches for pods with no node. It filters nodes by resources, taints, and affinity, scores the rest (spread across zones, bin-packing), and binds each pod to the best node.

walkthrough.title: Kubelet sees its pods
walkthrough.text: The kubelet on the chosen node watches for pods bound to it and starts working on the new one.

walkthrough.title: Run the containers
walkthrough.text: Through the container runtime interface (CRI), the kubelet pulls the image, sets up networking and volumes, starts the containers, and begins liveness and readiness probes.

walkthrough.title: Ready, then continue the rollout
walkthrough.text: Once the readiness probe passes, the pod joins the Service's endpoints and receives traffic. The controller then removes one old pod, which gets SIGTERM and a grace period, and repeats.

data.label: kubectl / GitOps

input.name: Status
input.type: rollout status: 2 of 3 updated replicas available

responsibilities: Declares the desired state rather than issuing step-by-step commands.
Keeps manifests in Git as the reviewed source of truth.
Watches rollout status and can undo to the previous revision.

failureModes.impact: Scheduler overpacks nodes; pods are OOM-killed under load.
failureModes.mitigation: Require requests and limits with admission policies.

failureModes.impact: Next GitOps sync reverts a hotfix unexpectedly.
failureModes.mitigation: All changes through Git; drift detection alerts.

data.label: etcd
responsibilities: Stores all cluster state consistently.
Provides watch streams that controllers rely on.
Survives minority member failures.

failureModes.impact: No writes: nothing can deploy or reschedule (running pods continue).
failureModes.mitigation: Odd member count across zones; regular snapshots and tested restores.

failureModes.impact: Leader elections and API latency spikes.

data.label: Controller Manager

output.name: Actions
output.type: Create RS v2, scale v2 up / v1 down

responsibilities: Repeatedly compares desired with actual state and corrects any gap.
Rolls out within maxSurge / maxUnavailable limits.
Pauses a rollout that stops making progress.

failureModes.impact: Rollout stalls halfway with mixed versions.
failureModes.mitigation: progressDeadlineSeconds marks failure; CD tooling rolls back.

failureModes.impact: No reconciliation: failed pods are not replaced.

data.label: API Server

input.name: Requests
input.type: REST + watch from users, controllers, kubelets

output.name: State
output.type: Persisted objects + watch events to subscribers

responsibilities: Is the only component that talks to etcd; everyone else uses it.
Authenticates, authorises (RBAC), and validates every change.
Fans out watch events so controllers react without polling.

failureModes.scenario: Admission webhook down with failurePolicy: Fail
failureModes.impact: All pod creations rejected; cluster cannot heal.
failureModes.mitigation: Highly available webhooks, timeouts, and exemptions for system namespaces.

failureModes.scenario: Too many LIST calls from a misbehaving client
failureModes.mitigation: API priority and fairness; informers with caches instead of polling.

data.label: Scheduler
responsibilities: Finds nodes with enough CPU and memory that satisfy constraints.
Spreads replicas across zones and nodes for resilience.
Leaves pods Pending with a reason if nothing fits.

failureModes.mitigation: Cluster autoscaler adds nodes; priority classes evict less important work.

failureModes.scenario: All replicas land in one zone
failureModes.impact: One zone outage takes the service down.
failureModes.mitigation: Topology spread constraints and pod anti-affinity.

data.label: Kubelet (per node)
responsibilities: Makes the node's actual pods match the pods assigned to it.
Runs liveness and readiness probes and restarts failed containers.
Handles graceful termination on scale-down.

failureModes.impact: Its pods are marked lost after a timeout.
failureModes.mitigation: Controllers recreate pods elsewhere; PodDisruptionBudgets for planned drains.

failureModes.impact: In-flight requests are cut off during rollouts.
failureModes.mitigation: Handle SIGTERM, preStop hooks, and an adequate grace period.

data.label: Container Runtime & Pods

output.name: Running pod
output.type: Containers with an IP, serving traffic

responsibilities: Pulls images and starts isolated containers.
Sets up the pod network and mounts volumes.
Enforces CPU and memory limits with cgroups.

failureModes.scenario: Image pull fails (bad tag, registry down)
failureModes.mitigation: Deploy by digest from a verified registry; pre-pull for large images.
Set limits from observed usage; alert on OOM kills.
